profile.scope: Separate 10-second 42000 messages/s diagnostic. Profiled latency excluded from reported benchmark results. CPU samples exclude kernel work. Scheduler deltas span monitor observations, including preparation and finish.
profile.first_attempt: Excluded: driver selected a short-lived perf helper PID and broke its stdout pipe. Retry selected the benchmark process and passed output validation.

limitations: One run per case, shared six-CPU host; no optimization winner or stable machine-independent latency claim.
5000 markets, 10000 books, 25 levels per side; smaller registry and connection population than full catalog.
Synthetic pre-generated JSON through real decoder, workers, and SBE writer; excludes WebSocket/TLS/discovery/capture.
Stage samples are per emitted level record from one in 67 input messages, including refresh corrections; sample messages may produce multiple records.
Receipt proxy is actual entry into decode_frame, excluding generator lateness; diagnostic timestamps are monotonic.
The M5 receive_to_encode field still uses scheduled arrivals and is labeled scheduled-to-encode in this report.
Added timestamp metadata changes message size; sparse sampling can miss a chunk rotation on the specific measured record. Complete all-record write timing and direct flush timing retain those stalls.
Controls use identical original source hashes but were run later, so host variation and probe overhead are not separable.
No speedup measurement or production code change was made.
reproduction_note: Recorded tool_sha256 identifies the original per-record diagnostic. The current reproduction tool supports batched output; recorded results are historical, not batching measurements.
